title: Community Resilience Microgrant
summary: Provides catalytic funding for neighborhood-led preparedness plans, micro-infrastructure upgrades, and resilience hubs that help coastal and rural residents withstand climate-driven floods, storms, and heat waves. Supports collaborative planning between residents, emergency managers, and local businesses to ensure culturally responsive response protocols. Encourages dissemination of preparedness toolkits and community drills that improve long-term hazard readiness.
eligibility: Registered nonprofit, community-based organization, or tribal entity with demonstrated local leadership
Project timeline under 24 months with clear milestones for preparedness and implementation
Documented partnerships with residents, emergency responders, or municipal agencies, including letters of support
Plan for community outreach and knowledge-sharing that can be replicated in similar geographies

title: Youth STEAM Innovation Fund
summary: Invests in afterschool and summer programs that integrate robotics, creative coding, digital storytelling, and design thinking to build confidence among youth innovators. Prioritizes initiatives that weave arts-based approaches into STEM competencies, especially for students historically excluded from technology careers. Supports cross-sector partnerships that culminate in public showcases, hackathons, or exhibitions elevating youth-led solutions.
eligibility: Serves youth ages 12-18 with intentional outreach to underrepresented genders and racial or ethnic groups
Operates in Title I school districts or equivalent low-income communities, with data demonstrating need
Program evaluation plan detailing qualitative and quantitative metrics, data collection methods, and reporting schedule
Evidence of mentorship model linking participants with college, industry, or artist mentors throughout the program cycle

title: Clean Energy Accelerator Grant
summary: Catalyzes community-scale solar, wind, and battery storage deployments paired with paid workforce training for residents transitioning from fossil fuel industries. Advances skills development through stackable credentials, apprenticeships, and employer commitments to hire graduates into living-wage clean energy careers. Encourages projects that integrate energy equity goals, demand forecasting, and measurable emissions reductions.
eligibility: Public-private partnership or consortium including community-based organizations, training providers, and employer partners
Project launches within 12 months and demonstrates site control, permitting milestones, and grid interconnection planning
Includes workforce training curriculum aligned with industry certifications and tracked job placement outcomes
Environmental justice impact assessment highlighting benefits to frontline or low-income communities

title: Health Equity Innovation Award
summary: Backs community-designed solutions that dismantle structural barriers to preventive care, mental health services, and chronic disease management for marginalized populations. Encourages projects combining culturally responsive care models, data-driven outreach, and co-created research with patient advocates. Funds pilot studies that identify scalable pathways to improve quality outcomes and reduce health disparities.
eligibility: 501(c)(3) status or fiscally sponsored initiative with documented governance structure
Serves historically marginalized groups such as Black, Indigenous, immigrant, LGBTQ+, or rural populations with limited care access
Formal partnership with local health providers, clinics, or health departments including a shared data plan
Evaluation design outlining patient or community advisory input, outcome measures, and dissemination strategy

title: Digital Literacy Expansion Fund
summary: Supports expansion of community computer labs, mobile device lending programs, and bilingual curriculum that equip learners of all ages with essential digital skills. Funds wraparound services such as broadband subsidies, hardware repair clinics, and digital navigation coaching. Prioritizes programs demonstrating long-term sustainability plans, intergenerational learning models, and strong local employer partnerships.
eligibility: Educational institutions, public libraries, or nonprofits with a demonstrated digital equity mission and active governance board
Ability to track learner progress through pre- and post-assessments, credential attainment, or employment outcomes
Partnership agreements with community stakeholders such as workforce boards, housing authorities, or school districts
Detailed implementation plan for accessibility accommodations and multilingual support

title: Local Food Systems Resilience Grant
summary: Advances regenerative farming, community-supported agriculture, and culturally relevant food distribution networks that shorten supply chains. Encourages food hubs integrating cold storage, aggregation, and cooperative marketing to stabilize incomes for small producers. Invests in farmer training, soil health data collection, and climate-smart infrastructure that enhance regional food sovereignty.
eligibility: Agricultural cooperatives, tribal food councils, or nonprofits with demonstrated experience in community-based food systems
Community partnership required, including letters of commitment from growers, distributors, and consumer organizations
Operating budget under $500,000 or clear plan showing how grant will leverage additional investments
Compliance with sustainable land stewardship standards and transparent reporting on distribution outcomes

title: Women in Tech Leadership Fellowship
summary: Empowers women and nonbinary technologists to access executive pathways through tailored leadership curricula, executive coaching, and venture-building labs. Provides peer learning cohorts, sponsorship opportunities with industry executives, and support for fellows launching impact ventures. Prioritizes models with measurable improvements in retention, promotion, and pay equity across partner organizations.
eligibility: Women-led or nonbinary-led organizations with at least one completed fellowship or cohort program demonstrating participant success
Mentorship component required, including structured matching, mentor training, and documented mentor engagement hours
Commitment to collecting longitudinal data on participant career advancement, compensation, and leadership outcomes
Policies ensuring inclusive recruitment of women of color, LGBTQ+ participants, caregivers, and professionals with disabilities

title: Arts for Social Change Grant
summary: Funds multidisciplinary art projects that elevate lived experiences of marginalized communities and catalyze civic dialogue. Supports public installations, participatory performances, and storytelling campaigns co-created with residents, activists, and cultural bearers. Encourages projects with policy or systems change goals and robust documentation plans to extend impact beyond the grant period.
eligibility: 501(c)(3) organization or fiscally sponsored collective with established artistic leadership
Public engagement activities required, including community design sessions, workshops, or performances with free access
Commitment to compensating artists, culture workers, and community partners equitably
Diversity of artists and project team members encouraged, including representation across race, age, disability, and language

title: Inclusive Entrepreneurship Fund
summary: Supports accelerators, incubators, and community finance programs that expand capital access and wraparound services for founders from underrepresented backgrounds. Backs technical assistance, procurement readiness, credit-building tools, and investor matchmaking tailored for minority-owned and women-led enterprises. Encourages data transparency on capital deployment, inclusive governance, and pathways to high-growth markets.
eligibility: Community-based organizations, accelerators, CDFIs, or chambers of commerce with proven track record serving underestimated founders
Must serve minority-owned or women-led startups with clear enrollment criteria and outreach strategy
Impact reporting required, including disaggregated data on capital deployed, revenue growth, and job creation
Commitment to anti-bias training for mentors, investors, and staff engaged in entrepreneur support services

title: Climate Tech Pilot Challenge
summary: Funds demonstration projects testing emerging climate technologies such as carbon capture, grid optimization, and nature-based solutions in real-world settings. Prioritizes pilots that quantify emissions reductions, community co-benefits, and commercialization potential. Encourages open science practices including data sharing, peer learning, and transparent measurement protocols.
eligibility: Research institutions, startups, or public-private consortia with technical expertise in climate mitigation technologies
Prototype, feasibility study, or field trial data demonstrating technical readiness level 5 or higher
Open data sharing policy detailing datasets to be released, privacy safeguards, and publication timelines
Letters of commitment from host sites, community partners, or utilities where pilots will be deployed

title: Accessible Education Infrastructure Fund
summary: Improves physical and digital learning environments through ADA-compliant renovations, assistive technology upgrades, and equitable design services. Supports projects modernizing classrooms, libraries, and community centers so learners with disabilities experience seamless participation. Encourages cross-sector teams that integrate universal design principles, student feedback, and post-implementation training for staff.
eligibility: Public or nonprofit educational institutions, library systems, or community learning centers with accessible facilities plan
Recent accessibility audit documentation required, outlining priority upgrades and compliance gaps
Implementation within 18 months with confirmed contractors, procurement processes, and maintenance budgets
Commitment to training educators and staff on inclusive technology use, accommodations, and emergency procedures

title: Community College Innovation Grant
summary: Supports community colleges piloting stackable credential pathways, applied research labs, and work-based learning aligned with AI, clean energy, advanced manufacturing, and healthcare sectors. Encourages integration of industry-grade equipment, modular curriculum, and wraparound student services. Funds collaborations that improve equitable access and lead to guaranteed interviews or apprenticeships with regional employers.
eligibility: Accredited community college or consortium of Florida institutions with established employer advisory boards
Industry or employer partnership required, including co-designed curriculum and commitments for student placement
Evaluation and student outcome tracking plan covering enrollment demographics, completion rates, earnings, and alumni progression
Evidence of student support services such as childcare, transportation assistance, or success coaching for adult learners

title: Public Health Preparedness Fund
summary: Enhances local health department capacity for pandemic response, biothreat detection, and climate-related health emergencies. Funds interoperable data systems, multilingual risk communications, and workforce training on incident command and community outreach. Supports partnerships with faith leaders, mutual aid networks, and school districts to ensure equitable emergency response.
eligibility: Health departments, tribal health agencies, or nonprofits working closely with public health authorities
Emergency preparedness focus documented through existing response plans and hazard risk assessments
Annual reporting requirement outlining drills conducted, response metrics, and lessons learned
Inclusion of community engagement strategy prioritizing vulnerable populations, including seniors, immigrants, and individuals with disabilities

title: STEM Education Access Challenge
summary: Expands equitable STEM access by funding teacher professional development, culturally relevant curriculum, and makerspace resources in under-resourced schools. Elevates STEM role models through mentorship networks, classroom residencies, and virtual industry tours. Encourages projects that measure student confidence, math and science proficiency, and persistence in advanced coursework.
eligibility: K-12 institutions, education nonprofits, or districts serving at least 50% underserved student populations
Teacher training plan required with calendar of workshops, coaching sessions, and ongoing support
Commitment to equitable resource distribution including accommodations for multilingual learners and students with disabilities
Data collection plan assessing student outcomes, educator skill growth, and family engagement

title: Sustainable Transportation Pilot Grant
summary: Funds pilots testing zero-emission transit, micromobility networks, smart traffic management, and safer active transportation corridors. Supports strategies co-designed with residents to reduce congestion, improve air quality, and increase multimodal access for low-income neighborhoods. Encourages alignment with Vision Zero policies, equitable fare structures, and transparent emissions tracking.
eligibility: Municipal or regional agencies, transit authorities, or metropolitan planning organizations with authority to deploy pilots
Environmental impact analysis required, including baseline emissions and projected reductions
Collaboration with transportation experts, community-based organizations, and accessibility advocates documented through MOUs
Plan for integrating pilot learnings into long-term infrastructure or policy changes with dedicated follow-on funding pathways

title: Veterans Career Advancement Fund
summary: Supports veteran-serving organizations offering skills translation, credential attainment, and career navigation tailored to military experiences. Funds wraparound supports such as mental health services, childcare, and housing stabilization to improve employment persistence. Encourages employer partnerships that create pathways into high-demand civilian careers and track long-term retention.
eligibility: Nonprofit serving U.S. veterans or military-connected families with documented governance and veteran leadership representation
Program must include career placement component with employer commitments and job coaching
Annual reporting required on participant demographics, credential attainment, employment outcomes, and wage progression
Evidence of trauma-informed services and referral networks addressing behavioral health, housing, and benefits navigation

title: Urban Greening Partnership Grant
summary: Invests in urban greening projects that expand tree canopy, restore vacant lots, and create climate-resilient park spaces co-designed with residents. Supports community stewardship programs, youth workforce crews, and environmental education campaigns. Prioritizes neighborhoods facing heat islands, flooding, and limited access to safe outdoor recreation.
eligibility: Municipal agency, community organization, or land trust with authority to implement improvements on public access land
Public access space required with ADA-compliant design and maintenance plans
Maintenance plan included covering staffing, irrigation, and long-term stewardship commitments
Community engagement strategy demonstrating resident leadership roles and culturally responsive outreach

title: Inclusive Arts Fellowship
summary: Provides stipends, production support, and professional development for artists with disabilities creating accessible performances, exhibitions, and digital media. Invests in organizations embedding disability justice principles into curatorial practices, employment, and audience engagement. Encourages the development of new assistive technologies, tactile experiences, and sensory-friendly programming.
eligibility: Individuals or arts organizations led by or centering artists with disabilities, including proof of accessibility accommodations
Accessibility plan required detailing tech tools, ASL interpretation, audio description, captioning, and sensory supports
Public engagement component ensuring community access through workshops, talkbacks, or open studio events
Documentation strategy for sharing inclusive practices with peer institutions and networks

title: Water Innovation Research Fund
summary: Supports applied research and demonstration projects advancing water recycling, leak detection, equitable rate design, and watershed restoration. Encourages collaboration with frontline communities to co-develop resilient infrastructure responding to droughts, floods, and contamination. Funds data-driven pilots that generate open-source tools and policy recommendations for utilities and regulators.
eligibility: Universities, research labs, or nonprofit institutes with expertise in hydrology, engineering, or environmental science
Pilot or demonstration required with field sites, instrumentation plans, and community engagement protocols
Partnership with local utility or water authority preferred, including cost-sharing commitments
Deliverables include peer-reviewed publications, data repositories, and policy briefs accessible to stakeholders

title: Rural Broadband Expansion Grant
summary: Expands high-speed broadband through fiber, fixed wireless, or open access networks that reach unserved farms, tribal lands, and remote main streets. Supports infrastructure planning, middle-mile construction, and affordability programs that ensure long-term adoption. Encourages projects that coordinate with federal funding, leverage crowd-sourced coverage data, and build local workforce capacity.
eligibility: Telecom providers, cooperatives, tribal entities, or local governments authorized to deploy broadband infrastructure
Feasibility study required including engineering designs, take-rate projections, and environmental review compliance
Completion within 3 years with phased construction schedule and risk mitigation plan
Affordability strategy demonstrating low-cost service tiers, digital literacy partnerships, and customer support for residents

title: Creative Youth Empowerment Fund
summary: Supports youth councils, student clubs, and school-based teams launching creative placemaking, media production, and social impact campaigns. Provides resources for young leaders to manage grants, collaborate with municipal agencies, and host public events showcasing community narratives. Emphasizes youth governance models that foster civic leadership and long-term cultural stewardship.
eligibility: Youth-led organizations or schools with documented youth governance structures allocating decision-making power
Ages 15-24 must lead the project, supported by stipends or leadership development resources
Adult mentorship required with clear roles for advisors, safety protocols, and safeguarding policies
Budget must include youth compensation, accessibility considerations, and community outreach strategy

title: AI for Social Good Grant
summary: Funds interdisciplinary teams deploying transparent, accountable AI systems that advance social, environmental, or humanitarian outcomes. Prioritizes applications that mitigate bias, protect privacy, and include impacted communities in governance. Supports prototyping, field testing, and open-source tools that translate ethical AI principles into measurable benefits.
eligibility: Academic, nonprofit, or startup organization with cross-functional team including domain experts and ethicists
Clear social impact framework with theory of change, risk mitigation plan, and community validation
Open-source component encouraged, including documentation, model cards, and reproducible datasets
Commitment to independent auditing, fairness testing, and public reporting on algorithmic outcomes

title: Neighborhood Safety and Design Grant
summary: Improves safety, walkability, and sense of belonging through resident-led planning that redesigns streetscapes, lighting, alleys, and gathering spaces. Supports tactical urbanism pilots, traffic calming installations, and placemaking that reduces violence without relying on punitive approaches. Encourages data-informed collaboration between neighborhood groups, planners, and youth leaders.
eligibility: Neighborhood associations, community development corporations, or nonprofits with fiduciary capacity
Resident participation required through design workshops, surveys, and steering committees reflecting community demographics
Local government support letter confirming alignment with zoning, permitting, and maintenance requirements
Safety plan integrating public health, restorative justice, or violence interruption partners

title: Senior Wellness Initiative Fund
summary: Supports aging service providers offering culturally responsive wellness classes, chronic disease prevention, and social connection programs for adults 60+. Funds transportation, telehealth coaching, and caregiver respite that reduce isolation and hospital readmissions. Encourages adoption of evidence-based models and technology tools that empower seniors to age in place safely.
eligibility: Nonprofits, community centers, or faith-based organizations serving adults 60+ with inclusive programming
Program design must incorporate physical, mental, and social wellness components grounded in evidence-based practices
Data collection plan tracking participation, health indicators, and social connectedness outcomes
Collaboration with healthcare providers, Area Agencies on Aging, or senior housing operators preferred

title: Environmental Justice Partnership Grant
summary: Funds frontline coalitions advancing community-led research, legal strategies, and policy campaigns that eliminate disproportionate pollution burdens. Supports organizing on clean air and water protections, industrial accountability, and equitable land use planning. Encourages power-building, multilingual communications, and leadership development for residents most impacted by environmental harms.
eligibility: Nonprofits, advocacy groups, or tribal governments with mission centered on environmental justice and community self-determination
Community leadership representation required in governance, staffing, and decision-making roles
Policy or systems change focus with articulated strategy, timeline, and targeted decision-makers
Commitment to participatory budgeting, transparent fund management, and safety protocols for organizers
